# 🚀 Next.js 15 Full Tutorial: From Zero to Production Next.js is a powerful React framework that gives you building blocks to create fast web applications. Unlike a plain React app, Next.js handles routing, optimization, and server-side rendering out of the box. --- ## 🛠 1. Prerequisites Before starting, ensure you have: - **Node.js 18.17** or later installed. - Basic knowledge of React (Check our [React Hooks Guide](/guide/react-hooks-guide-mnxs2a33)). - A terminal (Command Prompt, PowerShell, or Terminal). --- ## 📦 2. Automatic Installation The easiest way to start is using `create-next-app`. Open your terminal and run: ```bash npx create-next-app@latest my-next-project ``` **Recommended Settings:** - **TypeScript:** Yes (Recommended for better error catching) - **ESLint:** Yes - **Tailwind CSS:** Yes - **src/ directory:** No (Keep it simple for now) - **App Router:** **Yes** (Essential for modern Next.js) - **Import Alias:** Yes (@/*) --- ## 📂 3. Understanding the Folder Structure Next.js 15 uses the **App Router**. Here is how the files work: ```mermaid graph TD A[app/] --> B[layout.tsx - Global UI] A --> C[page.tsx - Home Page] A --> D[about/] D --> E[page.tsx - /about Route] A --> F[globals.css - Styles] ``` - **`layout.tsx`**: Used for UI that stays the same across pages (Navbar, Footer). - **`page.tsx`**: The actual content of the route. - **`public/`**: Static assets like images and fonts. --- ## ⚡ 4. Server vs. Client Components This is the most important concept in Next.js: 1. **Server Components (Default)**: Render on the server. Great for performance and SEO. They cannot use hooks like `useState`. 2. **Client Components**: Render in the browser. Use these for interactivity. Add `'use client';` at the very top of the file. ### Example of a Client Component: ```tsx 'use client'; import { useState } from 'react'; export default function Counter() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); return ( ); } ``` --- ## 🌐 5. Data Fetching In Next.js 15, fetching data is as simple as using `async/await` directly inside your Server Component: ```tsx // app/posts/page.tsx export default async function PostsPage() { const response = await fetch('https://api.example.com/posts'); const posts = await response.json(); return (

Blog Posts

{posts.map(post => (
{post.title}
))}
); } ``` --- ## 🚀 6. Deployment The best way to deploy Next.js is via **Vercel**: 1. Push your code to GitHub. 2. Import your repository into [Vercel](https://vercel.com). 3. It will automatically detect Next.js and deploy it for you! --- ## 📖 Learn More - **📖 Guide:** [React Hooks Guide](/guide/react-hooks-guide-mnxs2a33) - **📖 Guide:** [Introduction to JavaScript](/guide/مقدمة-في-javascript-mnxs2933)
